method: Manual source-aware review of four post-screen Chinese Jev laya cases. The labels describe visibility of the answer-bearing relation in the reconstructed first-60-character digest, not the model's internal knowledge or a causal effect.

cases.note: Digest shows Nate likes chocolate mousse and has made berry-containing cake, but the explicit preference for mixed berry flavor is only in memory 917b9dd4 after character 60. D3:10 directly states chocolate and mixed berry flavor preference.

Digest's first memory covers Saturday hiking with Audrey; its tail alone says Andrew has a Sunday picnic date with his girlfriend. D26:20 directly supports the latter. Other digest prefixes discuss different outings, not this Sunday date type.
Digest says James enrolled in cooking class but gives no lesson price. The $10 amount is after character 60 of memory b5e5b707; D23:15 directly says each class costs 10 dollars.

Digest first memory says Jolene read a book in late January but cuts before Snow Crash and its author; Sapiens remains visible at the beginning. D4:23 directly says she read Snow Crash two weeks before the February conversation. Answerer listed both titles, so old strict exact=false is not a Jev visibility label.
